theme.title: Quiet Session
theme.summary: Communication Svcs (+0.16%) and Technology (+0.12%) led the market today, while Consumer Discretionary (-0.27%) and Utilities (-0.25%) brought up the rear. Performance didn't cluster cleanly by style — growth averaged +0.00%, defensives -0.18%, and value/cyclicals -0.11% — more a stock-by-stock market than a single broad theme. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 -0.87%, Dow -1.32%, Nasdaq -1.00% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -1.34%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX fell 3.19% to 15.50, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold added 1.12% to $4,642.40, crude oil was little changed at $87.18, and bitcoin gained 5.22% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
